\section{Main Results}
\label{sec:results}

Vision token pruning in Vision Transformers (ViTs) is widely regarded as a reliable efficiency technique.
DynamicViT~\cite{rao2021dynamicvit} removes 30\%--50\% of tokens with less than 0.5\% accuracy loss on ImageNet, and Token Merging (ToMe)~\cite{bolya2023tome} merges up to 40\% of tokens while retaining over 99\% of classification accuracy.
EViT~\cite{liang2022evit} similarly discards 50\% of inattentive tokens with negligible degradation.
These results have motivated recent proposals to apply similar strategies to Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for real-time robotic control~\cite{hsu2025vlacache,wang2026vlaiap}.
Our experiments test whether this transfer holds: we apply six pruning configurations to a VLA policy and evaluate closed-loop Success Rate (SR) on the LIBERO benchmark~\cite{liu2023libero}.
The result is unambiguous.
Every configuration produces 0\% SR, a complete collapse we term the \emph{cliff edge}.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\caption{Ablation matrix across scoring functions, retention ratios, and pruning mechanisms. All six pruning conditions produce 0\% SR. The baseline runs the same checkpoint with pruning disabled (bypass mode). Wilson 95\% confidence intervals (CI) are computed over independent episodes. Experiment IDs are listed for reproducibility.}
\label{tab:ablation_matrix}
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}llccrrc@{}}
\toprule
Method & Scoring & $k$ & Mechanism & SR (\%) & Episodes & Wilson 95\% CI \\
\midrule
\textbf{Baseline} & \textbf{--} & \textbf{1.0} & \textbf{--} & \textbf{44.8} & \textbf{500} & \textbf{[40.5, 49.2]} \\
\midrule
ACIS & Learned & 0.5 & Zero-mask & 0.0 & 300+ & [0.0, 1.26] \\
ACIS & Learned & 0.7 & Zero-mask & 0.0 & 500 & [0.0, 0.76] \\
ACIS & Learned & 0.9 & Zero-mask & 0.0 & 500 & [0.0, 0.76] \\
Random & Random & 0.5 & Zero-mask & 0.0 & 500 & [0.0, 0.76] \\
ACIS & Learned & 0.5 & True removal & 0.0 & 500 & [0.0, 0.80] \\
ACIS & Learned & 0.5 & Merge & 0.0 & 500 & [0.0, 0.76] \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

Table~\ref{tab:ablation_matrix} presents the full ablation matrix.
We systematically vary three axes: (1)~the scoring function that selects which tokens to prune, (2)~the retention ratio $k$ that controls how many tokens survive, and (3)~the mechanism by which pruned tokens are handled.
The baseline achieves 44.8\% SR across 500 episodes using the identical model checkpoint with pruning disabled.
All six pruning conditions collapse to 0\% SR.

\paragraph{Scoring axis.}
If the failure were caused by a poor scoring function that discards the wrong tokens, replacing the learned Attention-weighted Cumulative Importance Score (ACIS) scorer with uniform random selection should produce a different outcome.
It does not: random pruning at $k{=}0.5$ also yields 0\% SR over 500 episodes (Table~\ref{tab:ablation_matrix}, row~5).
The cliff edge is therefore not a scoring quality problem.
No matter which tokens are selected for removal, the policy collapses.

\paragraph{Ratio axis.}
If the failure were caused by removing too many tokens, retaining 90\% of tokens ($k{=}0.9$, removing only 10\%) should preserve most task-relevant information.
Yet $k{=}0.9$ also produces 0\% SR (Table~\ref{tab:ablation_matrix}, row~3).
This rules out the hypothesis that a gentler pruning ratio would recover graceful degradation.
The transition from functional to non-functional is binary, not gradual.

\paragraph{Mechanism axis.}
Three distinct mechanisms for handling pruned tokens produce identical failure.
Zero-masking replaces pruned token embeddings with zeros, which could inject out-of-distribution (OOD) activation patterns.
True removal eliminates the tokens entirely, changing the sequence length but avoiding OOD injection.
Token merging (following ToMe~\cite{bolya2023tome}) combines pruned tokens with their nearest neighbors, preserving sequence length and total information.
All three mechanisms yield 0\% SR (Table~\ref{tab:ablation_matrix}, rows~2, 6, 7).
The collapse is therefore not caused by OOD activations from a particular masking strategy; it is a property of any alteration to the vision token sequence.

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{figures/paper/fig_cliff_edge.pdf}
\caption{The cliff edge in VLA token pruning. While ViT pruning methods retain $>$99\% accuracy on classification benchmarks even at aggressive retention ratios~\cite{rao2021dynamicvit,bolya2023tome,liang2022evit}, applying any form of token reduction to a VLA policy causes immediate collapse to 0\% SR across all LIBERO suites. \label{fig:cliff_edge}
\end{figure}

\section{Analysis}
\label{sec:analysis}

Section~\ref{sec:results} established that all pruning configurations produce 0\% SR.
This section investigates \emph{why} the cliff edge occurs.
We present three complementary lines of evidence: the LLM backbone attends to vision tokens near-uniformly (\S\ref{sec:uniform_attention}), pruning causes immediate single-step action failures rather than gradual error accumulation (\S\ref{sec:action_disruption}), and standard offline evaluation metrics fail to predict this catastrophic closed-loop collapse (\S\ref{sec:metric_disconnect}).
Section~\ref{sec:why_vit_works} synthesizes these findings into a unified mechanistic explanation.

\subsection{Uniform Attention Distribution}
\label{sec:uniform_attention}

Token pruning in ViT classifiers succeeds because attention concentrates on a small set of discriminative patches and leaves most tokens redundant.
DynamicViT~\cite{rao2021dynamicvit} and ToMe~\cite{bolya2023tome} exploit this concentration: tokens that receive low attention contribute little to the classification decision and can be safely removed.
We test whether VLA models exhibit the same attention pattern.

We extract attention weights from the LLM backbone (Qwen2-0.5B~\cite{yang2024qwen2}) over all vision tokens across three LIBERO tasks.
The attention entropy ratio reaches 0.98 (observed entropy of 6.86 bits out of a maximum of 7.0 bits for a perfectly uniform distribution).
The two camera views receive comparable attention (53.8\% for cam1, 46.2\% for cam2), and this pattern holds across all sampled tasks with entropy values between 6.844 and 6.846 bits.
The Gini coefficient of the attention distribution is 0.246, a value that confirms low inequality across tokens.
Figure~\ref{fig:attention_heatmap} visualizes this contrast.

The architectural explanation is straightforward.
SigLIP~\cite{zhai2023siglip} encodes images using non-overlapping spatial patches without a \texttt{[CLS]} aggregation token.
Each vision token therefore corresponds to a unique spatial region of the input image, and no two tokens encode the same information.
The VLA policy must predict precise continuous actions conditioned on the full spatial layout of the scene, so the LLM backbone attends broadly to recover the complete spatial context.
This stands in direct contrast to ViT classifiers, where a single discrete label can be derived from a subset of discriminative patches and the remaining tokens contribute marginal information.

The practical consequence is clear: when attention is uniform, no subset of tokens is dispensable.
Removing any group of vision tokens removes irreplaceable spatial information from the input, regardless of how those tokens are selected.

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{figures/paper/fig_attention_heatmap.pdf}
\caption{(a)~LLM attention over vision tokens in the VLA policy. The distribution is near-uniform (entropy ratio 0.98), with both camera views receiving comparable weight. (b)~Typical attention pattern in a ViT classifier (illustrative), where attention concentrates on a small set of discriminative patches. This concentration enables safe token pruning in classification but is absent in VLA action prediction.}
\label{fig:attention_heatmap}
\end{figure}

\subsection{Instantaneous Action Disruption}
\label{sec:action_disruption}

A natural hypothesis for the cliff edge is that small per-step errors compound over a long trajectory and eventually cause task failure.
We test this hypothesis by measuring single-step action errors under pruning, using the same observations and model checkpoint.

The results rule out gradual error accumulation.
Under the baseline (bypass mode, no pruning), the single-step L2 distance between predicted and ground-truth actions is 0.414.
Under pruning at $k{=}0.5$, this distance increases to 1.391, a 3.4$\times$ degradation.
The per-step relative error is 111.5\%; the error exceeds the magnitude of the action itself.
The failure is most severe in the gripper dimension, where the error of 1.02 indicates complete inversion: the policy commands the gripper to open when it should close, or vice versa.
Position dimensions show errors of [0.20, 0.25, 0.30] and rotation dimensions show errors of [0.01, 0.02, 0.01].

This is not a case where small errors compound into eventual failure.
A single pruned observation already produces a qualitatively wrong action.
The gripper inversion alone would cause immediate task failure in any manipulation task, independent of all subsequent steps.
Closed-loop trajectory analysis confirms this interpretation: the L2 divergence between pruned and baseline trajectories has a mean of 1.117, with onset at step~0.
The pruned policy diverges from the functional trajectory immediately, not after an accumulation period.
Figure~\ref{fig:action_divergence} shows the divergence curves.

These single-step measurements provide a direct causal link between vision token removal and action failure.
The cliff edge does not require temporal accumulation; it is instantaneous.

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{figures/paper/fig_action_divergence.pdf}
\caption{Trajectory divergence between pruned and baseline policies. The L2 distance is large from step~0 and remains elevated throughout the episode. The failure is instantaneous rather than the result of gradual error accumulation.}
\label{fig:action_divergence}
\end{figure}

\subsection{Offline Metric Disconnect}
\label{sec:metric_disconnect}

Standard practice in token pruning research is to validate a scoring function using offline metrics before deployment.
Our offline metrics provide consistently positive signals.
The importance margin gain (G1) shows a 93$\times$ improvement over the baseline, which indicates that the Attention-weighted Cumulative Importance Score (ACIS) learns to produce well-separated importance rankings.
The action loss ratio (G3) of 0.87 confirms that, on the training data distribution, the model's action loss with pruning is only 87\% of the full-token loss.
The Spearman correlation between ACIS scores and gradient magnitudes is 0.41, a moderate agreement between the learned importance scores and the gradient-based ground truth.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\caption{Offline evaluation metrics versus closed-loop performance. Offline ranking and loss metrics show positive signals, yet all pruning conditions produce 0\% closed-loop SR. The disconnect demonstrates that standard offline proxies are insufficient for validating VLA token compression.}
\label{tab:offline_vs_closedloop}
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lccr@{}}
\toprule
Metric & Result & Interpretation & SR (\%) \\
\midrule
Importance margin (G1) & 93$\times$ & Meaningful ranking & -- \\
Action loss ratio (G3) & 0.87 & Pruned $<$ full on train data & -- \\
ACIS-gradient Spearman & 0.41 & Moderate correlation & -- \\
\midrule
Single-step L2 (pruned) & 1.391 & 3.4$\times$ degradation & 0.0 \\
Relative action error & 111.5\% & Error $>$ action magnitude & 0.0 \\
Gripper error & 1.02 & Complete inversion & 0.0 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

Yet when pruning is actually applied, single-step action error is catastrophic: L2 of 1.391, relative error of 111.5\%, and complete gripper inversion (Table~\ref{tab:offline_vs_closedloop}).
The disconnect has a specific cause.
Ranking metrics (G1, Spearman) evaluate the quality of the importance ordering, not the effect of removing the lowest-ranked tokens.
A scorer can produce a perfect ranking yet still fail if every token carries critical information, because even the least important token may be indispensable for accurate action prediction.
The action loss ratio (G3) averages over the training set and masks the worst-case per-step errors that determine closed-loop success.
A ratio of 0.87 means the average loss increases by only 13\%, but the per-step relative error of 111.5\% reveals that the distribution of errors is heavy-tailed: the worst steps are far worse than the average suggests.

The failure cascade is consistent across all evaluation levels.
Offline ranking appears reasonable, offline action error is catastrophic, and closed-loop SR is 0\%.
This ordering implies that standard offline proxies (importance margins, averaged action losses, correlation coefficients) are necessary conditions for a good scorer but provide no guarantee of closed-loop viability.
Validating VLA compression requires closed-loop evaluation; offline metrics alone are insufficient.

\subsection{Why ViT Pruning Works but VLA Pruning Fails}
\label{sec:why_vit_works}

The three preceding analyses converge on a unified mechanistic explanation for the cliff edge.
The explanation rests on a fundamental difference between how ViT classifiers and VLA policies consume visual information.

In ViT classification, attention concentrates on a small subset of discriminative patches~\cite{rao2021dynamicvit,bolya2023tome,liang2022evit}.
The classification task requires a single discrete label from pooled features, so spatial completeness is not necessary.
Tokens outside the discriminative region carry redundant or irrelevant information, and their removal produces graceful degradation: accuracy decreases smoothly as more tokens are pruned, with less than 1\% loss even at 50\% token reduction.

In VLA action prediction, the situation is qualitatively different.
The attention distribution is near-uniform (\S\ref{sec:uniform_attention}), a direct consequence of the fact that precise continuous action prediction requires the complete spatial layout of the scene.
SigLIP~\cite{zhai2023siglip} encodes each non-overlapping spatial patch as a separate token with no \texttt{[CLS]} aggregation, so the VLA's LLM backbone must attend to all patches to reconstruct spatial relationships between the robot end-effector, target objects, and obstacles.

\section{Background}
\label{sec:background}

This section describes the two components of our experimental setup: the SmolVLA architecture~\cite{shukor2025smolvla}, in which we study vision token reduction, and the LIBERO benchmark~\cite{liu2023libero}, on which we evaluate closed-loop performance.

\subsection{SmolVLA Architecture}
\label{sec:smolvla_arch}

Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models cast robotic control as conditional generation: given a camera observation and a language instruction, the model predicts a continuous action.
SmolVLA~\cite{shukor2025smolvla} instantiates this paradigm with approximately 451.5M parameters, organized into a vision encoder, a modality connector, a language model backbone, and an action head.
Figure~\ref{fig:architecture} illustrates the full architecture and token flow.

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{figures/paper/fig_architecture.pdf}
\caption{SmolVLA architecture and token flow. Each camera image is encoded by SigLIP into 128 spatial patch tokens. An MLP connector projects these tokens into the LLM embedding space. The Qwen2-0.5B backbone processes the concatenated vision and language tokens, and a flow matching head generates continuous 7-DoF actions.}
\label{fig:architecture}
\end{figure}

\paragraph{Vision encoder.}
SmolVLA uses the Sigmoid Loss for Language-Image Pre-training (SigLIP) encoder~\cite{zhai2023siglip} to process visual input.
SigLIP divides each camera image into non-overlapping spatial patches and encodes them independently, producing 128 tokens per image.
Two properties of this encoding are relevant to our analysis.
First, SigLIP does not include a \texttt{[CLS]} aggregation token; there is no single summary representation that pools information across patches.
Second, because patches are non-overlapping, each token encodes a unique spatial region of the input image, and no two tokens carry redundant information.
These design choices mean that the 128-token output is a spatially complete, non-redundant representation of the scene.

\paragraph{Dual-camera input.}
SmolVLA receives images from two cameras: a wrist-mounted camera (cam1) and an overhead camera (cam2).
Each camera image produces 128 vision tokens through the SigLIP encoder, yielding 256 vision tokens total that enter the language model.
The two viewpoints are complementary: the wrist camera captures fine-grained end-effector interactions, while the overhead camera provides a global spatial layout of objects on the workspace.

\paragraph{MLP connector.}
A multi-layer perceptron (MLP) projects each SigLIP output token from the vision encoder embedding space into the Qwen2-0.5B embedding space.
This connector applies a learned linear transformation per token without cross-token interaction, preserving the one-to-one correspondence between spatial patches and tokens.
The intervention point for token reduction in our experiments sits immediately after this connector: pruning, masking, or merging operations are applied to the projected vision tokens before they enter the language model.

\paragraph{LLM backbone.}
The Qwen2-0.5B language model~\cite{yang2024qwen2} serves as the central reasoning module.
It receives a concatenated input sequence of 256 projected vision tokens and the tokenized language instruction.
Self-attention across this full sequence allows the model to ground language in visual context and to integrate information across both camera views.
The backbone must reconcile spatial relationships between the robot gripper, target objects, and obstacles using only the vision tokens, since no other spatial input is provided.

\paragraph{Flow matching action head.}
SmolVLA generates actions through conditional flow matching~\cite{lipman2023flow} rather than autoregressive token prediction.
The action head maps the LLM's output representation to a continuous 7-DoF action vector: three position coordinates, three rotation angles, and one gripper open/close value.
Flow matching learns a vector field that transports a noise distribution to the target action distribution, conditioned on the LLM output.
This formulation produces smooth, continuous actions suited to precise manipulation, but it also means that the action output depends holistically on the LLM's internal representation.
Any corruption of the vision token input propagates through the full LLM computation into the predicted action.

The overall inference pipeline proceeds as: image $\rightarrow$ SigLIP patches $\rightarrow$ 128 tokens per camera $\rightarrow$ MLP projection $\rightarrow$ concatenation with language tokens $\rightarrow$ Qwen2-0.5B forward pass $\rightarrow$ flow matching action prediction.
This architecture shares its high-level structure with larger VLA systems such as OpenVLA~\cite{kim2024openvla} and $\pi_0$~\cite{black2024pi0}, making SmolVLA a representative testbed for studying vision token efficiency in VLA policies.

\subsection{LIBERO Benchmark}
\label{sec:libero_bench}

We evaluate on the LIBERO benchmark~\cite{liu2023libero}, a suite of language-conditioned tabletop manipulation tasks in simulation.
LIBERO provides standardized task definitions, initial state distributions, and evaluation protocols for reproducible comparison of manipulation policies.
We use three of its four suites, each testing a distinct aspect of policy competence.
LIBERO-Object presents ten tasks focused on object manipulation; the policy must identify and interact with specific objects from visually similar alternatives.
LIBERO-Spatial presents ten tasks focused on spatial reasoning, where the policy must place objects correctly or navigate relative to reference locations.
LIBERO-Goal presents ten tasks with varied goal conditions applied to a shared environment layout; these tasks test whether the policy can condition its behavior on the language instruction.

Each suite contains 10 tasks, and we run 50 evaluation episodes per task, yielding 500 episodes per suite per experimental condition.
The evaluation metric is closed-loop Success Rate (SR): a binary indicator per episode that equals 1 only if the robot completes the full task within the time limit.
SR is measured through closed-loop execution, where the policy observes the current state, predicts an action, the simulator advances, and the policy re-observes the updated state at every timestep.
This closed-loop evaluation is critical because errors at any single step can cascade through subsequent observations and actions.
A policy that produces even one qualitatively wrong action (for example, opening the gripper when it should close) will likely fail the entire episode.

The three LIBERO suites span a range of baseline difficulty levels: SmolVLA achieves 44.8\% SR on Object, 51.8\% on Spatial, and 63.0\% on Goal in bypass mode (full vision tokens, no pruning).

# VLA-Pruner Paper Summary

Based on the provided abstract, here's what can be extracted:

**1. VLA Models Tested:**
The abstract indicates testing across "multiple VLA architectures" but doesn't specify which models in the excerpt provided.

**2. Pruning Approach:**
VLA-Pruner employs a dual-criterion strategy: semantic-level relevance through "vision-language prefill attention" and action-level importance via "action decode attention, estimated via temporal smoothing." This exploits "temporal continuity in robot manipulation."

**3. Benchmark Results:**
The abstract states the method "achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple VLA architectures and diverse robotic tasks" but specific benchmark scores aren't detailed in this excerpt.

**4. Evaluation Type:**
The abstract doesn't clarify whether evaluation is closed-loop or offline.

**5. Comparison with Attention-Based Methods:**
The abstract notes that existing "VLM-specific token pruning methods select tokens based solely on semantic salience metrics (e.g., prefill attention)" while overlooking action execution needs—implying VLA-Pruner differs from such approaches.

**6. Key Findings:**
The main insight is that semantic-focused pruning "bias token retention toward semantic cues, discard critical information for action generation" and degrade performance, which VLA-Pruner addresses through its dual-level approach.

*Note: The full paper PDF would contain detailed experimental results and comparisons.*

# EfficientVLA Paper Analysis

## 1. VLA Models Tested
The paper primarily evaluates **CogACT**, which combines DINOv2 and SigLIP vision encoders with a Llama2-7B language module and a Diffusion Transformer action head. They also test scalability across CogACT-Small, CogACT-Base, and CogACT-Large variants.

## 2. Token Compression Methods
Their approach uses three synergistic strategies:
- **Layer pruning** based on inter-layer similarity analysis
- **Visual token selection** balancing task relevance (via attention analysis) with feature diversity (cosine distance)
- **Feature caching** in the diffusion action head at fixed intervals

## 3. Main Results
On the SIMPLER benchmark with 22 LLM layers and 56 visual tokens:
- **1.93× inference speedup**
- **71.1% FLOP reduction** (down to 28.9% of original)
- **0.6% success rate drop** (74.8% → 74.2% average)
- Task-specific improvements: "Pick coke can achieved 94.0% vs baseline 91.3%"

## 4. LIBERO Evaluation
The paper does **not** evaluate on LIBERO. Testing occurs exclusively in the "SIMPLER environment" for tabletop manipulation tasks (pick, move, drawer operations).

## 5. Differentiation from Naive Pruning
Their approach outperforms random token dropping (20.9% success vs. 74.2%) by using "task-relevance and diversity-driven" selection, combining "high task relevance scores" with tokens maximally dissimilar from already-selected ones.

## 6. Key Finding on Token Reduction
Aggressive visual token pruning alone yields diminishing returns due to memory bottlenecks. The paper notes that "token-centric optimization methods...are inherently constrained by memory bounds."

# VLA-IAP 方法详细分析
# Paper Agent 调研笔记 — 2026-05-17

## 论文信息
- **Title**: VLA-IAP: Training-Free Visual Token Pruning via Interaction Alignment for Vision-Language-Action Models
- **arXiv**: 2603.22991
- **Year**: 2026

## 测试模型
- OpenVLA-OFT (7B, Llama-2 backbone + SigLIP + DINOv2 vision encoder)
- π₀ / π₀.₅ (PaliGemma-based, diffusion policy)
- DreamVLA (ViT + CLIP + DiT-B)
- **注意：未测试 SmolVLA (451M)**

## 核心方法

### 1. Geometric Prior (几何先验)
- 使用 **Sobel edge detection** 在灰度图上提取边缘强度
- "Structural anchors" = 纹理稀疏但结构关键的区域（如操作物体边界）
- Token importance = patch 区域内的平均边缘强度，归一化到 [0,1]
- **完全绕过模型内部 attention**，使用外部视觉几何特征

### 2. Dynamic Scheduling (动态调度)
- 计算 semantic intent mask 和 physical motion mask 之间的 IoU
- **Conservative mode** (IoU ≤ threshold): 保留所有非纯背景 token
- **Aggressive mode** (IoU > threshold): 只保留语义核心 + 运动区域 token
- **关键设计**: 在不确定阶段几乎不剪枝，只在高置信度状态才激进剪枝

### 3. Interaction-First Paradigm
- 核心论点: 基于 attention 的剪枝继承并放大了模型的感知错误
- "If the pre-trained model overlooks geometric details due to lack of physical continuity, pruning based on attention scores inherits and amplifies these errors"

## 主要结果 (LIBERO, OpenVLA-OFT)

| Retention | Spatial | Object | Goal | Long | Avg SR | Speedup |
|-----------|---------|--------|------|------|--------|---------|
| 100% (baseline) | — | — | — | — | **97.1%** | 1.00× |
| 70% | 97.6% | 99.6% | 98.4% | 95.6% | **97.8%** | 1.25× |
| 50% | 97.3% | 99.1% | 98.2% | 95.2% | **97.5%** | 1.37× |
| 30% | 96.6% | 98.8% | 98.0% | 94.8% | **97.1%** | 1.54× |

- 评估方式: **Closed-loop** on LIBERO (所有 4 个 suite) + real robot
- 对比 baseline EfficientVLA 在 70% retention 下降到 88.9%

## 与我们工作的关键差异

| 维度 | 我们 (SmolVLA + ACIS) | VLA-IAP (OpenVLA-OFT) |
|------|----------------------|----------------------|
| 模型大小 | 451M | 7B (~15x 大) |
| 基线 SR | 44.8% | 97.1% |
| 剪枝方法 | 基于 attention 的 learned scorer | 基于外部几何先验 (Sobel edge) |
| 动态调度 | 无 (固定 k 比例) | 有 (conservative ↔ aggressive) |
| Vision encoder | SigLIP only | SigLIP + DINOv2 |
| 结果 | 0% SR under ANY pruning | 97.8% SR at 70% retention |

## 为什么 VLA-IAP 能成功？(推测)

1. **模型能力余量**: 97.1% baseline 意味着模型高度过拟合任务，有更大的容错空间
2. **动态调度回退**: 在不确定阶段保留全部 token，实际平均剪枝比例可能远低于标称值
3. **外部几何信号**: Sobel edge detection 不依赖模型内部 attention（可能更可靠）
4. **双 vision encoder**: SigLIP + DINOv2 提供冗余视觉特征（DINOv2 的信息可能弥补 SigLIP token 被剪枝的损失）
5. **模型规模**: 7B 模型的 LLM backbone 可能对输入扰动更鲁棒

## 其他 VLA 效率方法 (搜索中发现)

- **EfficientVLA** (2025): Layer pruning + token selection + caching on CogACT (7B). 0.6% SR drop, 1.93x speedup. Tested on SIMPLER (not LIBERO).
- **VLA-Pruner** (2025): Temporal-aware dual-level (semantic + action attention). Multiple architectures.
- **VLA-ADP**: Action-aware dynamic pruning.
- **VLA-Cache** (NeurIPS 2025): Temporal KV caching (not removal). 1.7x speedup.

## Related Work positioning 建议

VLA-IAP 的成功不矛盾我们的 cliff-edge finding:
1. 我们展示 naive/attention-based pruning 在 SmolVLA 上完全失败
2. VLA-IAP 的成功依赖: (a) 外部几何先验, (b) 动态调度, (c) 更大模型, (d) 更强基线
3. 这恰恰证实了我们的核心洞察: VLA token reduction 需要 domain-specific 方法，不能简单迁移 ViT 的 attention-based pruning

若论文方向转为 B (positive contribution):
- 在 SmolVLA 上实现 geometric prior + dynamic scheduling，测试是否能解决 cliff-edge
- 关键问题: SmolVLA 44.8% baseline 的低容错空间是否允许任何剪枝？

# Introduction Narrative 两个方向草案
# Paper Agent 准备 — 2026-05-17

---

## Direction A: Pure Negative Results + "Smart Methods Needed"

### 故事线
ViT token pruning 在分类任务上成功 → 社区自然推广到 VLA → 我们系统测试发现 naive pruning 在 SmolVLA 上完全失败（cliff edge）→ 机制分析（attention uniformity + instantaneous disruption + offline metric disconnect）→ 启示：VLA token reduction 需要 domain-specific 方法（如 VLA-IAP 的几何先验 + 动态调度），不能简单迁移

### 贡献定位
- C1: 首次系统性 closed-loop 评估 VLA vision token reduction → cliff-edge 现象
- C2: 机制解释（为什么 ViT 可以但 VLA 不行）
- C3: Offline metric disconnect（标准验证流程不可靠）

### 优势
- 已有全部数据，无需新实验
- 叙事完整、逻辑自洽
- VLA-IAP 的成功反而加强而非削弱我们的论点（证实 smart methods 可行但 naive methods 不行）

### 风险
- Reviewer 可能认为 "只在一个小模型上的负结果" 泛化性不足
- "不 work" 的故事吸引力有限，缺少正面贡献
- VLA-IAP 已经展示了解决方案，审稿人可能问 "why not try VLA-IAP's approach?"

### Related Work 中 VLA-IAP 的定位
"Recent concurrent work VLA-IAP [Wang et al. 2026] reports successful VLA token pruning on OpenVLA-OFT (7B) using geometric priors and dynamic scheduling, achieving 97.8% SR at 70% retention. This result does not contradict our findings; rather, it confirms that VLA token reduction requires domain-specific methods with external geometric signals and adaptive scheduling, rather than the attention-based approaches that work for ViT classification. The success of VLA-IAP on a 7B model with 97.1% baseline SR does not guarantee that similar approaches transfer to compact VLAs (451M, 44.8% SR) where the model has less representational redundancy."

---

## Direction B: Negative Motivation + Positive Smart Compression

### 故事线
ViT token pruning 成功 → 应用到 VLA：naive methods 完全失败（cliff edge on SmolVLA）→ 分析为什么失败 → 基于分析洞察设计 smart compression → 跨模型验证（SmolVLA + OpenVLA）→ Smart compression 保持 SR 同时加速推理

### 可能的 Smart Compression 方法
1. **Geometric prior (仿 VLA-IAP)**: Sobel edge + structural anchor 保护
2. **Dynamic scheduling**: 根据 action uncertainty 动态调整保留比例
3. **KV cache reuse (仿 VLA-Cache)**: 时序连续帧的 vision token KV cache 复用
4. **Learned spatial pooling**: 训练时就学习将 256 → 128 tokens 的聚合
5. **Hybrid**: 静态区域 cache + 动态区域保留

### 贡献定位
- C1: Cliff-edge 现象 + 机制分析（motivation）
- C2: Smart compression 方法设计（基于我们的 attention uniformity 洞察）
- C3: 跨模型验证（SmolVLA + OpenVLA）

### 优势
- 有正面贡献，论文更有吸引力
- "问题 → 分析 → 解决" 的完整故事
- 跨模型验证提升泛化性

### 风险
- 需要大量新实验（OpenVLA 部署、smart compression 实现、调参、closed-loop eval）
- 时间紧张：CoRL abstract DDL May 26 (9天), paper DDL May 29 (12天)
- Smart compression 在 SmolVLA (44.8% baseline) 上可能仍然失败（模型容错空间太小）
- 与 VLA-IAP 的差异化不够明确

### 关键不确定性
- **SmolVLA 44.8% baseline 是否允许任何压缩？** 模型本身性能就不高，可能没有"可压缩的余量"
- **OpenVLA 部署可行性如何？** 需要 7B 模型的 GPU 资源 + LIBERO 环境适配
- **时间窗口够不够？** 12 天内做完新方法设计 + 实现 + 跨模型实验 + 论文重写

---

## 建议

**如果 OpenVLA 可行性调研 + smart compression 方案能在 3-5 天内完成原型**:
→ Direction B 值得尝试。但需要 fallback plan: 如果 smart compression 在 SmolVLA 上也失败，这个"连 smart methods 也失败"的结果反而让 negative result 更有说服力。

**如果时间不够或 OpenVLA 部署困难**:
→ Direction A 更安全。4 个章节已完成，只需补 Related Work + Discussion + Conclusion + Abstract，然后做 refinement。在 Discussion 中详细讨论 VLA-IAP 的成功和我们发现之间的关系，指出 model scale / baseline quality / geometric prior 的差异。

**Hybrid 策略**: 先走 Direction A 完成完整初稿（2天），同时 Agent 并行做 OpenVLA + smart compression 实验。如果实验有正面结果，在 paper DDL 前切换到 Direction B；如果没有，Direction A 已经 ready。
